idiom_name: circe Encoder/Decoder on the message case class plus an explicit mapper object
implementation_notes: The wire half is circe: the message is a separate case class whose Encoder/Decoder instances are written explicitly (Decoder.instance with c.downField("customer_id")), semi-derived, or - on Scala 3 - derives Codec, and the domain half is an OrderMessageMapper object with toMessage(order: Order): OrderMessage and fromMessage(m: OrderMessage): Order invoked by the endpoint (an Akka/Pekko consumer, a Kafka Deserializer). What replaces the classic mapper class is that object plus the codec instances in the message's companion; the implicit codec is only the wire layer, so no domain type may appear in the message case class.
pitfalls: Semi-automatic derivation keys on case-class field names: a wire rename then needs an explicit codec or configured member naming, and forgetting it fails at runtime instead of compile time.
Implicit codecs in a companion object are found everywhere: keep the domain-to-message mapper explicit so implicit search cannot serialise a domain type by accident.
Lazy or IterableOnce fields in the message shape complicate codecs and JSON output; map to concrete collections in the mapper.
circe's cursor-based decoding accumulates errors, but a wholly wrong shape still yields a decoder failure inside the consumer - route it to the invalid-message path deliberately.
